title: The blog post that never rots
body: The drawer of tools I never use holds a strange power. It promises a solution for every problem I might have someday. Most blogs are like that drawer. They publish an article and then hope it survives the next platform update, the next algorithm, the next decade. Let's measure it. How much of what we read online will vanish when the servers shut down. The numbers held are not in our favor. A blockchain post is different. It is not a promise. It is a fact. Once published, it exists. It cannot be taken down. It cannot be altered. This permanence changes what we can build. Imagine a recipe blog where the measurements are locked in stone. No more broken cakes because of a typo in the flour amount. Or a legal guide where the citations are permanent and verifiable. You can check them tonight. The text is just one part. What about the embedded images? A blog post can show a photo of a contract, but you cannot prove it is real. On-chain, you can embed a legal document, a receipt, a piece of art. The image becomes part of the record. It is not just decoration. It is evidence. Then there are the tables. A blog can display a table, but it is a picture of a table. It is not functional. On-chain, a table is alive. It is data. You can sort it, filter it, use it. A price history is not just a story. It is a tool. A list of ingredients is not just text. It is a checklist. This is not about making blogs better. It is about building something new. Something that lasts. Something that can be trusted. The next time you see a drawer full of potential, think about what you would build if you knew it would never disappear.
